questions.q: What question does statistical anomaly detection answer more sharply than a fixed hardcoded threshold?
options: Whether a value is unusual given everything else you've seen, rather than just outside a hardcoded number
Whether the pipeline has finished running
Whether the source system is online
Whether the data has been backed up
questions.explain: Anomaly detection isn't a new pipeline stage — it sharpens the same real-time data quality checking with a statistical basis for 'unusual.'

questions.q: What does the z-score method assume about the metric it's checking?
options: That the metric is roughly normally distributed around a mean
That the metric always increases over time
That the metric has no relationship to a mean or standard deviation at all
That the metric can only take positive values
questions.explain: Z-score flags values more than about 3 standard deviations from the mean, which only makes sense if the distribution is roughly bell-shaped.

questions.q: Why might a z-score check on daily row counts produce false alarms for a table with a strong weekday/weekend pattern?
options: Because the pattern breaks the roughly-normal-distribution assumption the z-score method depends on
Because z-score cannot be computed on integers
Because weekday and weekend data are stored in different tables
Because z-score only works on streaming data, not batch data
questions.explain: A strong recurring pattern isn't a simple bell curve around one mean, so z-score's assumption doesn't hold and normal variation gets flagged.

questions.q: What is the key conceptual advantage of isolation forest over z-score, per this lesson?
options: It makes no distribution-shape assumption and can flag anomalies across multiple metrics at once
It is always faster to compute than a z-score
It requires no data at all to run
It replaces the need for any human review of flagged results
questions.explain: Isolation forest builds random partitions and flags points that separate out in few splits — no normal-distribution assumption, and it handles multiple metrics together.

questions.q: What role does AI play in this lesson's anomaly detection workflow?
options: It helps draft the statistical check as code or explain a flagged result in plain language — it doesn't decide what counts as anomalous
It replaces the need for z-score or isolation forest entirely
It automatically fixes any anomaly it detects without review
It determines the business meaning of an anomaly without human input
questions.explain: The statistics still decide what's anomalous; AI speeds up writing and explaining the check, consistent with the multiplier framing from Lesson 43.
